text: The patient is a 72-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension. She presents with a 3-day history of progressive shortness of breath and orthopnea. Physical examination reveals bilateral crackles in the lung bases and 2+ pitting edema in the lower extremities. Chest X-ray shows cardiomegaly with pulmonary vascular congestion. Diagnosis is acute exacerbation of congestive heart failure.

A 58-year-old male presents with sudden onset of severe left-sided headache. Neurological examination reveals mild left-sided weakness and facial droop. Non-contrast CT head shows no acute intracranial hemorrhage. The patient is started on antiplatelet therapy and admitted for stroke workup.

Patient is a 45-year-old female with no significant past medical history. She presents with right lower quadrant abdominal pain that has been worsening over 24 hours. Physical exam reveals tenderness at McBurney's point with rebound. CT abdomen shows a dilated appendix with surrounding fat stranding. Diagnosis is acute appendicitis. The patient is taken emergently for laparoscopic appendectomy.

A 68-year-old male with COPD presents with worsening productive cough and fever. Sputum culture grows Streptococcus pneumoniae. Chest X-ray reveals a right lower lobe infiltrate. The patient is started on appropriate antibiotics and shows improvement within 48 hours.

Patient is a 35-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of ulcerative colitis. He presents with bloody diarrhea and abdominal cramping. Colonoscopy shows continuous inflammation extending from the rectum to the descending colon. The patient is started on mesalamine therapy. His symptoms gradually improve over the next several weeks.

A 52-year-old female presents with a 3-week history of fatigue and easy bruising. Complete blood count reveals thrombocytopenia with a platelet count of 45,000. Bone marrow biopsy shows normal cellularity with increased megakaryocytes. Diagnosis is immune thrombocytopenic purpura. The patient is started on corticosteroids and her platelet count improves.

Patient is a 77-year-old female with osteoarthritis who fell at home. She presents with right hip pain and inability to bear weight. X-ray shows a displaced femoral neck fracture. The patient is scheduled for hemiarthroplasty.

A 62-year-old male with a history of smoking presents with hematuria. CT urogram reveals a 3 cm mass in the right kidney. The patient undergoes partial nephrectomy. Pathology confirms renal cell carcinoma.

Patient is a 28-year-old female with 3 days of fever and severe headache. She reports neck stiffness and photophobia. Lumbar puncture reveals elevated white blood cells and low glucose. The patient is admitted for treatment of suspected bacterial meningitis.

A 70-year-old male presents with a 6-month history of progressive memory decline. His family reports episodes of confusion and difficulty with daily tasks. Neurological examination shows mild cognitive impairment. MRI brain reveals hippocampal atrophy consistent with Alzheimer's disease.

Patient is a 55-year-old female with obesity presenting with right upper quadrant pain. The pain is postprandial and radiates to the right shoulder. Ultrasound demonstrates multiple gallstones with gallbladder wall thickening. The patient undergoes laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

A 48-year-old male with hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with chest pain. The pain is substernal and occurs with exertion. Stress test reveals reversible ischemia in the anterior wall. Cardiac catheterization shows 80% stenosis of the LAD artery. The patient undergoes successful angioplasty with stent placement.

Patient is a 32-year-old male with 2 weeks of fatigue and swollen joints. He reports morning stiffness lasting more than an hour. Rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies are positive. The patient is started on methotrexate and shows improvement in symptoms.

A 65-year-old female with osteoporosis presents with new-onset back pain. She reports a minor fall 2 weeks ago. MRI shows an acute compression fracture at T12. The patient is started on pain management and physical therapy.

Patient is a 42-year-old male with a history of epilepsy presenting with breakthrough seizures. His medication levels were found to be subtherapeutic. He reports missing several doses of his seizure medication. His medication dosage is adjusted and he is counseled on adherence.

A 75-year-old male with dementia presents with a 2-day history of confusion and agitation. Urinalysis shows evidence of a urinary tract infection. The patient is started on antibiotics and his confusion gradually improves.

Patient is a 50-year-old female with a thyroid nodule found on routine exam. Thyroid ultrasound shows a 2.5 cm hypoechoic nodule with calcifications. Fine needle aspiration reveals suspicious cells for papillary carcinoma. The patient undergoes total thyroidectomy.

A 38-year-old male presents with acute knee pain and swelling after a basketball game. He reports hearing a pop at the time of injury. MRI reveals a complete ACL tear. The patient is scheduled for ACL reconstruction surgery.

Patient is a 60-year-old female with a history of breast cancer presenting with new bone pain. She reports the pain is worse in her lower back and hips. Bone scan reveals multiple lesions suggestive of metastatic disease. The patient is started on palliative radiation therapy.
A 25-year-old female presents with a 1-week history of fever and sore throat. Rapid strep test is positive. The patient is treated with amoxicillin. Her symptoms improve after 48 hours of treatment.

Patient is a 67-year-old male with chronic kidney disease presenting with nausea and vomiting. Laboratory tests reveal a creatinine of 4.2 mg/dL, up from 2.8 mg/dL. The patient is admitted for management of acute kidney injury. His symptoms resolve with intravenous fluids and monitoring.

A 55-year-old male presents with a 3-month history of progressive difficulty swallowing. He reports that solid foods are getting stuck in his chest. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy reveals a stricture in the distal esophagus. The stricture is dilated and biopsy reveals no malignancy.

Patient is a 33-year-old female with anxiety presenting with palpitations. Holter monitor shows episodes of supraventricular tachycardia. The patient is started on a beta-blocker and reports improvement in symptoms.

A 70-year-old female with a history of atrial fibrillation presents with acute confusion. She is found to have a rapid ventricular rate of 150 beats per minute. The patient is started on amiodarone and her symptoms improve.

Patient is a 40-year-old male with a history of gout presenting with acute toe pain. He reports the pain started suddenly in the middle of the night. Physical exam reveals a swollen, red, warm first metatarsophalangeal joint. The patient is started on colchicine and symptoms improve within 24 hours. He is counseled on dietary modifications and medications to prevent future flares.
